messages.content: What is the change in entropy in Joules per Kelvin of a 1kg ice block at 0°C if it is heated to 100°C under 1 atmosphere of pressure?

function.name: entropy_change_calculate
function.description: Calculate the change in entropy for a mass of a specific substance under set initial and final conditions. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

substance.description: The substance for which the change in entropy is calculated.

mass.description: The mass of the substance in kg.

initial_temperature.description: The initial temperature of the substance in degree Celsius.

final_temperature.description: The final temperature of the substance in degree Celsius.

pressure.description: The pressure the substance is under in atmospheres.

message.reasoning:
We need to calculate entropy change for heating ice from 0°C to 100°C under 1 atm. But we have to consider phase changes: ice at 0°C to water at 0°C (melting), then water from 0°C to 100°C, then water to steam at 100°C (boiling). The question says "ice block at 0°C heated to 100°C under 1 atm". So we need to compute ΔS = ∫ dQ_rev/T. For each stage: melting at 0°C: ΔS_melt = ΔH_fus / T (T=273.15 K). Then heating water from 0°C to 100°C: ΔS_water = ∫ C_p_water dT / T. Then boiling at 100°C: ΔS_vap = ΔH_vap / T (T=373.15 K). Use standard values: ΔH_fus for water ~ 6.01 kJ/mol; ΔH_vap ~ 40.79 kJ/mol. Molar mass of water 18.01528 g/mol. For 1 kg = 1000 g = 55.51 mol. So ΔS_melt = 55.51 * 6.01 kJ/mol / 273.15 K = (55.51*6.01)/273.15 kJ/K. Compute: 55.51*6.01 = 333.7 kJ. Divide by 273.15 gives 1.222 kJ/K = 1222 J/K.

ΔS_water: need integral of Cp/T from 0°C to 100°C. Cp of water ~ 75.3 J/(mol·K) at 25°C but varies. We can approximate using average Cp ~ 75 J/(mol·K). Then ΔS_water ≈ 55.51 * 75 J/mol/K * ln(373.15/273.15). Ln ratio: ln(373.15/273.15)=ln(1.367)=0.313. Multiply: 55.51*75=4163 J/K. Times 0.313 = 1304 J/K.

Alternatively use more accurate Cp values: but approximate.

ΔS_vap: ΔS_vap = 55.51 * 40.79 kJ/mol / 373.15 K = (55.51*40.79)/373.15 kJ/K. 55.51*40.79=2265 kJ. Divide by 373.15 gives 6.07 kJ/K = 6070 J/K.

Sum: 1222 + 1304 + 6070 = 8596 J/K.

But we might need to include the latent heat of fusion and vaporization. Let's compute more precisely:

Use ΔH_fus = 6.01 kJ/mol, ΔH_vap = 40.79 kJ/mol. Use Cp water = 75.3 J/(mol·K). Ln ratio: ln(373.15/273.15)=0.313. So ΔS_water = 55.51*75.3*0.313 = 55.51*23.58 = 1309 J/K.

So total ΔS = 1222 + 1309 + 6070 = 8601 J/K.

Thus answer ~ 8600 J/K.
